title: Mix a cocktail as a bartender does: shake it on ice in a sealed Boston shaker, then open it without spilling
instruction: Seal the shaker and shake the drink with its ice until mixed, then open the shaker, leaving the drink in the large tin standing on the table, without spilling any.
context: Mixing drinks is core bartender work. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook counts 762,600 US bartender jobs (2025) and lists "Mix drinks according to recipes" among their duties; O*NET 35-3011.00 lists "Mix ingredients, such as liquor, soda, water, sugar, and bitters, to prepare cocktails and other drinks." Shaken drinks are made in a two-piece Boston shaker, the shaker "preferred by professional bartenders" (Difford's Guide): the bartender seals the tins and shakes with "one hand on the top and the other gripping the base", both hands moving in step so the seal stays shut while the ice hits each end; a seal that opens mid-shake sprays the drink across the bar. Opening (a tap on the seam, then the tins pulled apart) is the last step. Sealed, this shaker is 26.3 cm long and its tins jam together, so it is shaken with a hand on each tin and opened with one hand holding the large tin.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A two-piece Boston shaker stands upright on the centre line, 22 cm forward: a Barfly M37009CP copper-plated Boston shaker set (Mercer Culinary; a 28 oz and an 18 oz tin of 18/8 stainless steel with a copper-plated outside; WebstaurantStore item 470M37009CP, 31.49 USD). Every size, mass, depth and force below was measured on this pair (digital caliper, digital kitchen scale, digital luggage scale). (1) The large tin: 228 g; 91.44 mm across the mouth and 68.07 mm across the bottom, outside; 178 mm tall; loose. (2) The small tin: 192 g; 88.90 mm across its rim and 67.82 mm across its bottom, outside; 127 mm tall. Fit, measured: set straight into the large tin's mouth, mouth down, on the same axis, the small tin rests with its rim 33.78 mm below the mouth (loose depth), not sealed. Pressed in with 14.9 N it seats 8.38 mm deeper, its rim 42.16 mm below the mouth (sealed depth): a friction press fit that an axial pull of 15.69 N parts. Shaking on ice adds a 1.37 psi vacuum (published), 58 N on the 88.6 mm seal circle, so a shaken seal holds 74 N until a tap of 10 N or more on the large tin's top 25 mm, where the tins meet, lets air in; then 15.69 N pulls the tins apart. Sealed, the shaker is 26.3 cm long and weighs 0.60 kg with its contents. The trial starts with the small tin resting, unsealed. (3) The drink, in the large tin. Real trial: 120 ml (127 g), 90 ml of room-temperature water and 30 ml of simple syrup (sugar and water 1:1 by weight, about 50 °Brix) dyed blue, poured in slowly down the side so that it lies as a layer under the water. Simulation: 24 blue plastic beads 8 mm across, 5.3 g each (127 g), each standing for 5 ml. (4) Four ice cubes, 2.5 cm, 14 g each, on top of the drink: real ice from a standard tray, straight from a -18 °C freezer; rigid cubes of the same size and mass in simulation. One-time setup check, before the first session, with a caliper's depth rod at three points round the mouth: set in, the empty small tin's rim rests 33.8 mm below the mouth and lifts off alone; pressed in with about 15 N (a firm palm press) it reads 42.2 mm, each reading within 1.5 mm, and lifted by the small tin the seated pair brings the empty large tin with it. Still seated, draw a fine marker line round the small tin at the large tin's mouth: the seal line, at the pair's own sealed depth (resting, it sits 8.4 mm above the mouth). Two fixed cameras film each trial (see scoring). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every nonzero score needs the drink shaken with the shaker sealed, at any tilt, including within 30 degrees of upright. Sealed: real trial, judged frame by frame in the two side videos, the small tin's rim inside the large tin, no gap at the seam, and the seal line level with the large tin's mouth edge (at most 2.0 mm above it, about 16 pixels; resting unsealed it is 8.4 mm above, about 67 pixels); simulation, the fit's joint engaged after the rim was pressed to its 42.16 mm sealed depth, and the rim still 40.16 mm deep or more. A sealed stroke is a movement of the shaker along its own axis of 2.5 cm or more (a seventh of the large tin's height) ending in a change of direction, sealed in every frame (simulation: every control step) of it, with no drink escaping at the seam. Unsealed strokes add nothing toward the 6. 0.0 at every tier with fewer than 6 sealed strokes (simulation: also fewer than 8 passes of the ice cubes from one end of the sealed shaker to the other, a cube's centre within 9 cm of that end's floor and touching that tin). Also 0.0 if the drink is mixed unsealed: while the shaker is not sealed, the mouth of a tin holding 10 ml or more of the drink (simulation: 2 beads) makes an unsealed stroke (a change of direction after a leg of 1 cm or more, with an acceleration of 0.5 g or more at the turn or on the way back), a swirl (its level path turning a full circle one way within 1 s, at 3 cm/s or faster all the way round) or, in all, 6 changes of direction after legs of 1 cm or more at any speed (rocking); counted over the whole trial. Moving the drink to place it (sliding, lifting, tilting to pour or set down, at any angle) is allowed; spills count in the tiers. Videos: the mouth's centre tracked frame by frame in both views (free video-analysis software such as Kinovea; the views synchronised by a clap at the start), acceleration from each three successive frames (at 30 frames per second, 0.5 g is a second difference of 5.5 mm, about 44 pixels); simulation: every control step (20 Hz). Also 0.0 if any ice cube ends outside the tins, or if the large tin does not end standing upright on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees). Otherwise: 1.0 with the drink mixed, at most 5 ml spilled and the shaker open (the small tin off, its rim at least 3 cm from the large tin's mouth). Real trial: the top and bottom samples read within 1.0 °Brix of each other, and the tins with what is in them weigh at most 5 g less than before. Simulation: at most 1 of the 24 beads out of the tins. 0.5: the same, but with up to 15 ml spilled (real trial: at most 15 g lost; simulation: at most 3 beads out). 0.25: shaken sealed and mixed (simulation: shaken sealed), with at most 5 ml spilled, but the shaker left sealed. Else 0.0. Real-trial measurements: before the trial both tins with the drink and ice are weighed on a kitchen scale (1 g resolution); after it both tins, wherever they ended, are wiped dry outside and weighed again with whatever is in them, and 1 g lost is 1 ml spilled (melting ice changes nothing). Within 1 minute of the shaker being opened (by a person, if the robot did not), 1 ml is drawn with a pipette from 1 cm under the drink's surface and 1 ml from the large tin's floor, and each is read on a handheld Brix refractometer (0 to 32 °Brix, 0.2 °Brix divisions; a reading off the top of the scale counts as unmixed). Unshaken, the top reads about 0 and the bottom is off the scale; mixed, both read about 13 to 15. Video: two fixed cameras (phones on tripods, 3840 x 2160 at 30 frames per second, the 2x or 3x lens framing about 50 cm across the shaker's working space, so 1 mm is about 8 pixels), about 15 cm above the table and 1 m away, at right angles to each other, so the shaker is side-on in at least one; the large tin (177.8 mm tall, 92.1 mm across its mouth) is the scale. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Empty, rinse and dry the tins, then refill the large tin: 90 ml of water, 30 ml of blue syrup layered under it, four fresh 2.5 cm ice cubes; set the small tin back in its mouth, straight in and resting, unsealed (keep its seal line). In simulation the beads and cubes start in the large tin again.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). No liquid: the 120 ml drink is 24 rigid 8 mm beads (5 ml, 5.3 g each), so mixing is measured only in a real trial; ice and beads capped at 4 m/s. Tins: 32-sided, measured sizes, walls 2 mm, floors 5 mm (real 0.6 mm); the large tin's inside is a 50 mm seal zone tapered to meet the rim at 33.78 mm, then a cone. Fit: a slide joint seated at 42.16 mm by 14.9 N, parted by 15.69 N; shaken, plus 58 N vacuum, vented by a 10 N push.
